title: Converting Your NRO Account to Resident: A Step-by-Step Guide
description: Upon returning to India and becoming a resident, it is mandatory to convert your NRO account to a resident savings account. This conversion is a regulatory re.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to convert my NRO account?
faq.a: Yes, it is mandatory to convert your NRO account to a resident savings account once you return to India and your residential status changes from NRI to Resident Indian as per FEMA regulations.

faq.q: What happens if I don't convert my NRO account?
faq.a: Failure to convert your NRO account can lead to non-compliance with FEMA regulations. Your bank might freeze the account, impose penalties, or restrict transactions until the conversion is completed, causing significant inconvenience.

faq.q: Can I continue to hold my NRO fixed deposit?
faq.a: No, your NRO fixed deposit must also be converted to a resident fixed deposit. The bank will typically convert it at the existing interest rate until maturity, but future renewals will be at resident FD rates.

faq.q: What documents are typically required for conversion?
faq.a: Commonly required documents include a filled conversion form, proof of Indian address (Aadhaar, utility bill), proof of identity (PAN, Passport), passport-sized photos, and a declaration of your return to India.

faq.q: How long does the NRO account conversion take?
faq.a: The conversion process typically takes 5-10 working days after all required documents are submitted and verified. However, this can vary based on the bank and the completeness of your documentation.

faq.q: Will the interest rate on my NRO fixed deposit change after conversion?
faq.a: Generally, the interest rate on your NRO fixed deposit will remain the same until its maturity date. Upon renewal, it will be converted to a resident fixed deposit and will earn interest at the prevailing resident FD rates.

Your NRE account cannot continue as an NRE account. You have the option to convert it to a Resident Foreign Currency (RFC) account to hold foreign currency or convert it to a regular resident savings account in Indian Rupees.
